hero.title: A complete e-commerce journey built as a deployable portfolio case study.
hero.description: NOVA Market is a responsive Flask application that connects catalogue discovery, customer accounts, a server-priced cart, delivery selection, Stripe Sandbox Checkout, signed webhook processing, and order history in one coherent flow.
hero.status: Live portfolio demo · Stripe test mode
hero.disclaimer: NOVA Market is a technical portfolio demonstration. Products, customer details, and orders are fictional. Stripe runs exclusively in sandbox mode, and the application does not accept commercial orders or provide fulfilment services.

overview.title: Project Overview
paragraphs: NOVA Market explores the engineering work behind a modern e-commerce journey rather than presenting only a visual storefront.

The application connects a responsive interface to a Flask backend, PostgreSQL persistence, server-controlled pricing, authenticated sessions, and Stripe Sandbox Checkout. Payment confirmation is processed through a signed webhook before local order state is updated.

problem.title: Problem
problem.body: A checkout flow has to coordinate state across the browser, application, database, and payment provider without trusting client-supplied prices or assuming that redirects prove payment.
items: Keep product prices, delivery costs, currency, and totals under server control.
Connect authentication, cart state, delivery selection, payment, and order history.
Process asynchronous payment confirmation safely and idempotently.
Protect public authentication and checkout operations from abuse.
Remain transparent about the fictional catalogue and sandbox-only payment scope.

solution.title: Solution
solution.body: I built a modular Flask application with separate layers for routes, business rules, persistence, payment integration, security controls, and rate-limit storage.
items: Trusted product data and delivery rules are reloaded from PostgreSQL before checkout.
Stripe Checkout Sessions are created from server-calculated EUR totals.
Signed webhook events are matched against the local order, amount, currency, and Session ID.
Versioned SQL migrations and idempotent catalogue seeding control database initialization.
PostgreSQL-backed counters share rate-limit state across application processes.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.body: Cloudflare provides authoritative DNS only. Application and webhook traffic terminate at Render before reaching Gunicorn and Flask.
architecture.dnsAriaLabel: The browser resolves the NOVA Market domain through Cloudflare authoritative DNS, which returns the Render target.
architecture.dnsNote: Cloudflare is configured as DNS only and is not an application proxy.
architecture.appAriaLabel: The browser sends an HTTPS request through the Render custom domain to Gunicorn, Flask, and Neon PostgreSQL.
architecture.stripeAriaLabel: Stripe sends a signed webhook through Render and Gunicorn to Flask verification and Neon PostgreSQL.

security.title: Security and Reliability
security.body: The public deployment uses layered, security-conscious controls:
items: scrypt password hashing, CSRF protection, and secure production cookies
server-controlled prices, delivery fees, totals, and EUR currency
parameterized PostgreSQL queries and case-insensitive e-mail uniqueness
Content Security Policy, trusted-host validation, and baseline security headers
Stripe test-key enforcement and signed webhook verification
idempotent Checkout Session creation and payment confirmation
PostgreSQL-backed rate limiting with HMAC-SHA256 client identifiers
fail-closed responses when shared rate-limit storage is unavailable

payment.title: Payment Flow
steps: The customer reviews products and selects a delivery option.
Flask reloads trusted product prices and calculates the EUR total.
A local pending order and its items are stored in PostgreSQL.
Flask creates a Stripe Sandbox Checkout Session from trusted values.
The browser completes the test payment on Stripe-hosted Checkout.
Stripe sends a signed event to the webhook endpoint.
Flask verifies the signature, amount, currency, Session ID, and order reference.
The local order is updated idempotently and displayed in account history.
payment.note: The application never handles card details directly.

livingStartpakke.title: Living Startpakke — Research-led Product Discovery
livingStartpakke.subtitle: An independently led digital product concept exploring how critical everyday knowledge about a person can be made easier to access, understand, and keep up to date across families and care environments.
livingStartpakke.statusStatement: Living Startpakke is a research-led, user-informed concept currently in product discovery. It is not a finished product, working application, or validated solution.
livingStartpakke.status: Clickable concept prototype ready for feedback

facts.label: Focus
facts.value: Product discovery, user research, insight analysis, and prototyping

problem.title: Problem, Context and Boundaries
problem.body: Critical everyday knowledge about a person can be distributed across documents, routines, family members, and experienced staff. New or temporary staff may not have quick access to current, practical guidance about communication, preferences, triggers, routines, and everyday support.
items: Families may need to repeat the same practical information when new people become involved.
Teams can become dependent on the memory of experienced staff.
Existing information may be difficult to find, outdated, or unsuitable for the moment it is needed.
The concept focuses on people who communicate with limited or no spoken language and the people supporting them.
problem.boundaryBody: The concept is not intended to replace medical records, formal care plans, professional assessments, or existing documentation systems.

discovery.title: Discovery Approach and Evidence Base
discovery.body: I initiated the project and continue to lead it independently, while collecting input from relatives, care workers, professionals, and relevant stakeholder environments. Discovery began before a technical solution was defined, to understand whether the main issue was missing information, outdated information, limited access, or ineffective use of existing information.

evidence.label: Qualitative interviews
evidence.body: Family, school, and residential care perspectives.

evidence.label: Expert input
evidence.body: One expert and contextual conversation with a relevant specialist environment, presented anonymously.

evidence.label: Stakeholder environments
evidence.body: Included in outreach or landscape mapping across disability support, communication, family support, education, and municipal care. Identities are not published.

discovery.note: The evidence base is still developing. These activities inform the direction of the concept but do not constitute full product validation. No organization, expert, respondent, or location is identified publicly.

research.title: Research Themes and Direction Change

themes.title: Knowledge can be fragmented
themes.body: Important information may be spread across documents, conversations, personal experience, and informal routines.

themes.title: Information is often repeated
themes.body: Relatives and experienced staff may need to explain the same practical details repeatedly.

themes.title: Documentation is not always sufficient in the moment
themes.body: Relevant information can be difficult to find, too extensive, outdated, or poorly suited to a new worker.

themes.title: Prioritization matters
themes.body: New staff need a clear view of what matters before a first interaction, not every available detail at once.

research.directionBody: Discovery shifted the concept from a static start package toward a living and maintainable knowledge concept focused on prioritization, recency, and controlled access.
research.directionNote: Research also indicated a need to separate stable knowledge from short-term updates instead of mixing both into one undifferentiated information view.

prototype.title: Prototype
prototype.body: A clickable concept prototype was created in Figma to explore the proposed MVP scope using fictional data. The complete interactive prototype remains private during the feedback process.

views.title: Person card
views.body: Explores a prioritized view of practical information that may matter before a first interaction.

views.title: Timeline
views.body: Explores how recent updates, upcoming events, observations, and stable knowledge could remain distinct.

views.title: Access concept
views.body: Explores role-based visibility, editing responsibility, and temporary access to sensitive information.

prototype.interactionsBody: The prototype also explores read confirmation, quick note capture, voice notes, and temporary access.
prototype.limitation: The prototype demonstrates design hypotheses, not implemented functionality. There is no working application, production code, database, authentication system, or backend.

current.title: Current Stage, Open Questions and Constraints
current.body: The clickable concept prototype is ready for feedback, and initial feedback outreach is underway. No usability, adoption, or product-value claims are made at this stage.
current.questionsTitle: What has not yet been verified
questions: Which information is genuinely essential before a first interaction?
Can people find and understand that information quickly?
How should short-term updates and long-term knowledge be separated?
Who should maintain the information and be accountable for its quality?
Which access roles and temporary-access rules are realistic?
What privacy, consent, and security requirements would apply?
How could the concept fit alongside existing documentation systems?
constraints: The prototype can test comprehension and workflow assumptions, but not production security or technical integration.
Feedback results are not yet sufficient to describe the concept as validated, pilot-ready, or ready for implementation.
Private research materials, raw responses, interview content, and the full prototype are not published.

risks.title: Risks and Next Steps

items.title: Sensitive information
items.body: Any implementation would require careful decisions about privacy, consent, access control, and accountability.

items.title: Information quality
items.body: Outdated, incomplete, or incorrectly prioritized information could reduce trust and create additional risk.

items.title: Maintenance responsibility
items.body: The concept depends on current information, but ownership of updates has not yet been verified.

items.title: Organizational fit
items.body: The concept would need to support existing professional routines rather than create another disconnected system.

nextSteps: Collect and analyze the first round of structured prototype feedback.
Refine information hierarchy, wording, navigation, and interaction hypotheses.
Conduct focused follow-up conversations where responses require clarification.
Refine the proposed MVP scope based on recurring patterns in the evidence.
Investigate information ownership, consent, privacy, access rules, and compatibility with existing documentation.
Consider technical implementation only after the main workflow and responsibility assumptions have stronger evidence.

jarvis.title: JARVIS — Private AI Automation Environment
jarvis.subtitle: An operational OpenClaw-based workspace for research, persistent context, scheduled monitoring, and everyday technical automation.

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Environment design, integration, automation, and operations

facts.label: Infrastructure
facts.value: Self-managed Ubuntu VPS on Hetzner · ARM64

problem.title: Problem
problem.body: Research, infrastructure notes, project decisions, and job-search materials were distributed across tools and short-lived AI sessions.
items: Useful context was easy to lose between sessions.
Repeated research created unnecessary work.
Technical and product materials lacked one structured workspace.
Routine monitoring and organization still required manual attention.

usage.title: Current Use
usage.body: JARVIS supports practical work rather than acting as a general-purpose automation platform.
items: Technical and product research.
Job analysis and structured opportunity reviews.
Research reports and competitive analysis.
Project documentation and context retrieval.
Approved Git operations and maintenance tasks.
Resource monitoring and memory workflows.

openClaw.title: What OpenClaw Provides
openClaw.body: OpenClaw provides the core gateway and runtime. JARVIS is a deployed, configured, and extended private environment—not an agent platform built from scratch.
items: Gateway and isolated sessions.
Tool and skill execution.
Built-in semantic memory search.
Telegram integration.
Extensible plugin architecture.
openClaw.note: Planner workflows and MCP integrations are available platform directions but are currently outside this project’s scope.

contribution.title: My Contribution
contribution.body: My work focuses on environment design, integrations, operational workflows, and safe day-to-day use.
items: Deployed and configured OpenClaw on a self-managed VPS.
Integrated DeepSeek V4 Pro and Telegram access.
Defined workspace rules, memory structure, and research workflows.
Configured isolated scheduled resource-monitoring and memory workflows.
Built a custom REST service and portfolio middleware for separate use cases.
Configured CORS, Cloudflare Tunnel transport, and selected supporting services.
Documented safe Git operations and maintenance procedures.

memory.title: Persistent Context and Memory
memory.body: The current file-based memory and built-in semantic search are sufficient for the present scope, so an external vector database has not been introduced.
items: Long-term summary for stable context.
Dated daily memory notes.
Session history and project files.
Structured research reports.

automation.title: Automation
automation.body: A scheduled isolated workflow is configured to run daily at 23:55 CEST. It creates a dated memory note and updates the long-term summary when execution completes successfully. Longer runs can approach the configured timeout limit.
items: Server resource monitoring runs every six hours.
Alerts are configured for resource usage above 80%, but an incident-triggered path has not yet been tested end to end.
Scheduled tasks run in isolated sessions to limit context overlap.
automation.note: Resource monitoring runs on schedule, while the daily memory-summary workflow is configured and monitored with known timeout limitations.

deployment.title: Deployment and Operations
items: SSH key access and UFW firewall rules.
Docker for selected supporting services.
System service configuration for selected supporting services.
Resource monitoring and scheduled maintenance workflows.
Cloudflare Tunnel for the portfolio integration path.
Manual operational review where automatic recovery is not yet available.

security.title: Security Boundaries
items: SSH key-based administration and firewall restrictions.
Cloudflare Tunnel instead of exposing the portfolio middleware directly.
Restricted CORS configuration for the public integration.
Private repository and protected environment configuration.
Private workspace data excluded from Git.

reliability.title: Current Limitations
items: Automatic gateway recovery is incomplete.
Backup automation is not yet implemented.
Model requests do not use a custom retry layer.
End-to-end health monitoring and workflow tests remain limited.

outsideScope.title: Currently Outside the Project Scope
outsideScope.body: The file-based memory and built-in semantic search meet current needs; adding more infrastructure without a demonstrated requirement would increase complexity.
items: External vector database.
MCP integrations.
Interactive multi-agent orchestration.
Multi-step planner workflows.

results.title: Operational Results
results.body: The outcomes are qualitative and operational; no SLA, ROI, or time-saving claim is presented without measured evidence.
items: Job and market research is captured in reusable structured reports.
Competitive research and the KnowMe benchmark remain accessible in one workspace.
Persistent project context can be retrieved across sessions.
Resource monitoring runs on a defined schedule.

nextSteps.title: Next Steps
items: Complete automatic gateway recovery.
Introduce encrypted backup automation.
Review memory-workflow timeout behavior.
Add health checks and failure notifications.
Add a custom retry strategy for model requests.
Expand end-to-end workflow tests and monitoring.
Evaluate MCP only where a concrete integration need appears.
Prepare sanitized public technical documentation.

pwnedProject.title: Pwned Password Check
pwnedProject.desc: Check whether a password has appeared in data breaches. The backend uses the k-Anonymity method with Have I Been Pwned, so the full password is never sent.
pwnedProject.archDesc: The backend exposes an API endpoint that accepts a password, generates its SHA-1 hash, and communicates with the HaveIBeenPwned API to check whether the password has appeared in data breaches.
pwnedProject.connectionError: Could not connect to the backend.
pwnedProject.checkFailed: The password could not be checked.
pwnedProject.how1: The backend calculates the SHA-1 hash of the password and sends only the first 5 characters to the API.
pwnedProject.how2: HaveIBeenPwned returns a list of matching hashes and the number of times they appear.
pwnedProject.how3: The backend compares the remaining part of the hash locally and returns the result.

auth.title: Auth & User Management API
auth.desc: Authentication backend with JWT login, role-based access, PostgreSQL persistence, and protected API routes.
auth.archDesc: The project consists of a FastAPI backend that handles user registration, login, and access to protected endpoints. User data is stored in a PostgreSQL database using SQLAlchemy, and passwords are secured with bcrypt hashing. After successful login, the backend generates a JWT token used to authorize subsequent requests, and access to selected resources is controlled based on the user’s role, such as admin or user.
auth.tokenMissing: Use demo credentials to test the authentication flow.
auth.tokenOk: JWT token active — requests include Authorization: Bearer token.
